kpis.sub: NRC ISSUES TVA CLINCH RIVER BWRX-300 CONSTRUCTION PERMIT
kpis.label: The NRC approved a construction permit (Sep 29-30) for TVA's 300 MW GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 at Clinch River, TN — completed in 14 months, four months ahead of schedule, and only the second US advanced-reactor construction permit in a decade after TerraPower's Natrium (Mar 2026); but it authorizes construction only, TVA has disclosed no cost, start date or financing partner, and the only timeline is a 2032 operating target

Announced Sep 30: a 20-year agreement covering 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs (Maryland), supporting about $3B of upgrades that add roughly 190 MW of new capacity between 2030 and 2032 and underpin a 20-year licence extension — contracted, priced cash flow from an existing fleet rather than a framework agreement

kpis.sub: TERM URANIUM PRICE HITS A 19-YEAR HIGH
kpis.label: The long-term contract price passed 2007's $95/lb peak (spot ~$88/lb), yet nuclear equities kept falling: through Oct 2 Oklo is down ~50% YTD, NuScale ~45%, Cameco ~7% and the VanEck NLR ETF ~16%, as utilities balk at sticker prices (term contracting volume down ~15% YoY to just over 38M lb through Aug 31) and hyperscalers want megawatts in 2027, not gigawatts in 2037

The Clinch River permit moves the first US grid-scale SMR from 'pending' to 'permitted', but nothing is under construction yet and TVA reportedly still needs a co-investor; the earliest operating target remains 2032, so the gap between a licence and a delivered reactor is unchanged this week

rows.angle: Largest US nuclear fleet operator (55 GW post-Calpine); direct data-center PPAs with Microsoft, Meta, Walmart, now Amazon
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 2 at $257.49 (market cap ~$92.5B; 52-week range $228.63–$412.70) after the Sep 30 Amazon deal — a 20-year, 690 MW Calvert Cliffs PPA backing ~$3B of upgrades and ~190 MW of new capacity by 2030–32; shares jumped as much as 6.4% on Oct 1 before paring to ~+2%; Q2 adjusted EPS $2.55 with full-year guidance raised to $11.50–$12.50, and the 22-analyst consensus target of $347.28 implies ~35% upside; Crane (TMI-1) restart still targeted for 2027

rows.angle: Major Western uranium producer + 49% of Westinghouse
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 2 at $85.18 (down ~7% YTD, ~37% below the $135.24 high) even as the long-term uranium price hit a record $96/lb; the squeeze is on valuation and timing — trailing P/E ~149, forward ~52, Q1 realized price only $65.45/lb, utilities hesitant to sign new term contracts, a $559M Canadian tax dispute and possible US tariffs; the Westinghouse IPO remains undated, with reports pointing to a public filing as early as October and valuation estimates still ranging from ~$22B to $50B+

rows.angle: Nuclear components, naval reactors, advanced reactor work
rows.watch for: Investor Day (Sep 29) set 2030 targets of $5.5–$6.0B revenue (from ~$3.8B in 2026), $1.1–$1.2B adjusted EBITDA (~20% margin) and $525–$575M free cash flow, on an $8.4B backlog (up from ~$4B) that includes a $1.63B depleted-uranium contract and a $1.5B enrichment initiative; shares were ~$137 on Oct 1, still ~43% below the $241.82 high, and Northland trimmed its FY27 EPS estimate to $5.02 from $5.17 (Outperform, $220 target) on Sep 30 — the market has not yet rewarded the targets

rows.angle: Grid equipment + BWRX-300 SMR design via GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy
rows.watch for: Shares closed at $962.49 on Sep 29 (+6% over the month) as the NRC issued the first US construction permit for the BWRX-300 at TVA's Clinch River site — 14 months from application, four months early; TVA still needs a co-investor (possibly a data-center operator) to fund construction, and nuclear remains a small slice of a company priced mainly on grid and gas-turbine demand; GEV is also held in the Energy Storage sleeve, so avoid double-counting

rows.angle: Fast reactors using recycled waste; Sam Altman-backed; deals directly with AI/data-center customers
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 2 at $37.94 (+2%; down ~50% YTD), well below the $77 area the stock traded at in May after the NRC approved its Aurora principal design criteria; Q2 delivered the company's first revenue ($1.2M) while the ~$1B at-the-market program remains a dilution overhang, and the Eielson AFB microreactor selection and ~2,100MW of mostly non-binding customer pipeline are validation rather than contracted revenue; first deployments are guided to late 2027 or 2028

rows.angle: Only SMR design with NRC formal approval; utility-focused; 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 framework (non-binding)
rows.watch for: Shares rose ~4% to $8.07 on Oct 2 (down ~45% YTD) but the underlying story is dilution: the company has sold ~90M shares for nearly $985M via at-the-market programs, authorized a new program of up to $750M, and its diluted share count is up ~173% YoY (~133M to ~365M); Q2 ended with ~$1.9B of cash and investments, but there is still no binding TVA power purchase agreement (management targets year-end 2026) and the Clinch River permit this week went to GE's BWRX-300, not NuScale's design; RoPower (Romania) is the other near-term catalyst

rows.angle: HALEU enrichment — fuel for advanced reactors
rows.watch for: Shares closed Oct 2 at $139.27, within ~3% of the $135.75 52-week low (the high was $464.25) and down ~53% in market cap to ~$2.85B; contract backlog is $3.0B (up from $2.3B at year-end 2025) against 2025 revenue of ~$449M, and the 19-analyst consensus target of ~$247 sits ~78% above the price; HALEU deliveries under the Radiant and Antares contracts do not begin until 2030 and a GAO report found no national-security mission requiring 'unobligated' HALEU

private_watchlist.name: Holtec Nuclear

bear_case.title: Record uranium prices, falling nuclear stocks
bear_case.description: The term uranium price broke a 19-year record at $96/lb, yet Oklo is down ~50% YTD, NuScale ~45%, and even Cameco ~7% — the fuel-price thesis is working while the equity thesis is not. Utilities are reluctant to contract at these prices (term volume -15% YoY), so higher prices may be delaying demand rather than confirming it. Counter: a record term price means producers' realized prices (Cameco's was only $65.45/lb in Q1) have room to catch up.

bear_case.title: A permit is not a reactor
bear_case.description: The Clinch River approval obligates TVA to build nothing: no cost, start date or financing partner has been disclosed, a co-investor is still needed, and the only timeline is a 2032 operating target. TVA spent hundreds of millions on a Clinch River breeder reactor from the 1970s that was never completed. Counter: the NRC finished the review four months early, which is a genuine improvement in licensing speed.

bear_case.title: Dilution is funding the story
bear_case.description: NuScale's diluted share count is up ~173% in a year, with a new $750M at-the-market program on top of ~$985M already raised; Oklo carries a ~$1B program against $1.2M of first-ever revenue. Holders are being diluted to pay for commercialization that is years away. Counter: NuScale reports ~$1.9B of cash and investments, which removes near-term financing risk.

bear_case.title: Timing mismatch with hyperscaler demand
bear_case.description: Data-center operators need megawatts in 2027, but new SMRs are a 2030s story; Amazon's Calvert Cliffs deal (190 MW of new capacity only by 2030–32) shows even the best-positioned operator is selling existing output and uprates. Counter: those uprate and restart deals (Crane 2027) are the near-term supply and are going to the operators, not the pre-revenue developers.
